introduction: On this Sunday, God speaks through Hosea like a husband who wants to win back his unfaithful bride, promising to betroth her to himself forever in love and faithfulness. In the Gospel, Jesus calls himself the bridegroom, and says that new wine needs fresh wineskins. Paul tells the Corinthians that they are a letter from Christ written on human hearts. Let us open our hearts to the new life Christ brings.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abundant in loving kindness. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church, the bride of Christ: that she may be faithful to her bridegroom. Let us pray to the Lord.
For married couples: that their love may reflect God's faithful and tender love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have wandered from God: that they may hear him speak tenderly to them and return. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who fast and pray: that they may long for the bridegroom with open hearts. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that our lives may be a letter of Christ, written by the Spirit of the living God. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you love your people as a bridegroom loves his bride. Renew our hearts like fresh wineskins, so that we may receive the new wine of your Son's life. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The bridegroom is with them
reflection.body:
The prophet Hosea describes God's love for his people in the language of marriage. Israel has been unfaithful, but God does not give up. He says, "I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak tenderly to her." And he makes a promise: "I will betroth you to me forever." God's love is not only that of a ruler or a judge; it is the love of a faithful spouse.

In the Gospel, people ask why Jesus' disciples do not fast like the disciples of John and the Pharisees. Jesus answers with the same image: "Can the groomsmen fast while the bridegroom is with them?" He is the bridegroom Hosea spoke of: God himself, come to be with his people. While he is with them, it is a time of celebration. Jesus adds that the day will come when the bridegroom is taken away, and then they will fast. The Church has seen here the origin of Christian fasting, especially on Fridays and in Lent.

Then Jesus gives two images of newness. No one sews new, unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. And "No one puts new wine into old wineskins." Old wineskins have lost their flexibility; new wine, still fermenting, would burst them. Instead, "they put new wine into fresh wineskins." The life Jesus brings is new, and it needs hearts that are open and flexible, not rigid and closed.

Paul says something similar to the Corinthians: they themselves are a letter from Christ, "written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tablets of stone, but in tablets that are hearts of flesh." And he adds, "the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life."

This week, ask God where your heart has become rigid, like an old wineskin. And thank him for his faithful love, which never gives up on you.
